# dsh-custom-env
English | 中文
Community DeepSeek Harness plugin for managing environment variables in **Settings → Environment**.
Not an official DeepSeek AI product.
Changes apply to the running app right away, and on Windows / macOS also to the user environment so
new terminals can see them. Linux user-environment sync is not supported.
## Install
Requires DSH with the `dsh` CLI (`desktop` or `web`).

## For users

1. Open **Settings → Environment**
2. Edit a row as a draft → **Confirm** to save, **Cancel** to dis

card
3. **Groups** (accordion) are UI/plugin labels only — they do not change `process.env` / OS syn
c. `.env` stays `NAME=value`; group metadata is `$DSH_HOME/.dsh-custom-env-groups.json`. Create / re

name / delete groups from the headers; move a saved row with **Move to group**
4. Paste `NAME=VALUE`
lines into an empty row to add or update several variables at once (same names overlay existing row

s as drafts and keep their group)
5. Drag across rows to multi-select, or Ctrl/Cmd+click to toggle;

Ctrl/Cmd+C copies selected rows as `NAME=VALUE` (input text selection still wins when present)
6. **

Restore** brings back the value from when this app session started
7. At startup, values are injecte
d into the Host `process.env` first; writing the user environment (registry / launchctl) is deferred
via `setImmediate` into a child process and is not broadcast. Log off or reboot before other tools

need those values
8. Use **Install** only when shown, to wire this Host’s `dsh` command into your us
er PATH (Windows / macOS)

### When saving a value
| You save | Variable does not exist yet | Variable already exists |

| A non-empty value | Created | Replaced |
| An empty value | Created as empty | Left unchanged |
## For other plugins (Remote API)
Call the Host `customEnv` service (`ctx.get('customEnv')` or injected `ctx.customEnv`).
